messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: service-discovery-core (P1) - elevated SRV lookup error rate in us-west-2b. Alerts: 350 errors/min, error budget burn. Paging on-call.
eric: i’m oncall — paging in. seeing SRV failures in prod? where are errors spiking exactly?
mike: infra here. metric heatmap shows SRV SERVFAILs coming from pods in us-west-2b talking to consul cluster. consul raft heartbeats dropping between nodes in us-west-2b <-> us-west-2a. network retransmits up ~12%.
jess: coreDNS logs also show a bunch of NXDOMAIN/SERVFAILs for internal SRV queries, negative caching looks saturated. example (from a failing pod):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.12-Ubuntu <<>> _api._tcp.myservice.namespace.svc.cluster.local SRV +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
```
eric: ok — is this a pure consul issue (gossip/raft) or a coredns config problem?
mike: looks upstream — consul leader is flapping. I'm seeing repeated leader elections every ~20s in the logs. suspected cause: intermittent packet loss across us-west-2b VPC router. traced to a noisy network node in the AZ.
tara: ops reported a network maintenance window earlier but it was supposed to be low-impact. i'm checking cloud provider health.

deploy-bot: aws-notify: AWS reported a brief networking disruption in us-west-2b starting 2026-09-10T02:35Z affecting some AZ egress paths.
jess: that maps to our incident window. mitigation options: 1) reduce cross-AZ raft pressure (increase heartbeat/tick settings), 2) pin consul leader to a healthy AZ temporarily, 3) restart coredns pods to clear negative cache.
eric: prioritize actions that reduce customer impact quickest — do a coredns rolling restart in the troubled AZ and try to stabilize consul leader. mike, can you force a leader in us-west-2a?
mike: yes. plan: set consul maintenance on the flaky nodes (to stop elections), promote node consul-uw2a-01 as leader by patching raft config (force-leader), then bump heartbeat from 50ms->120ms temporarily. executing now.

mike: running commands:
```
kubectl -n consul exec -it consul-uw2a-01 -- consul operator raft list-peers
kubectl -n consul patch statefulset consul --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"--raft-heartbeat=120ms"}]'
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-2b
```
deploy-bot: Started rolling restart of coredns in us-west-2b (3 pods).
jess: after killing one coredns pod we see caches repopulating and SRV SERVFAIL rate dropping by ~60% in that AZ. good.
eric: monitor consul leader status and SRV latency. mike, any sign of split-brain?
mike: no split-brain. leader now stable on consul-uw2a-01. raft election frequency dropped to baseline. network still noisy but less impact after leader pin and heartbeat bump.
support-bot: customer-impact update: initial blast affected ephemeral connections for internal service discovery. We saw retries/backpressure cause higher 5xx for orchestration clients. Affected: 3 tenant clusters in us-west-2 with elevated errors between 02:35Z - 03:17Z (~42 minutes). Notifying CSMs for ChattyCo and DataShip (top accounts).
eric: any data loss?
mike: no persistent data loss in consul KV. service registrations briefly missing but re-registered after reconnection.
jess: follow-ups: 1) revert force leader once we have safer cross-AZ connectivity checks, 2) add conservative raft timeouts per-AZ so single AZ flaps don't cause cluster-wide elections, 3) add coredns config tweak to avoid long negative caching on SRV failures, 4) add a specific alert for consul election rate + SRV error correlation.
tara: ops is opening a ticket with cloud provider for the AZ router node; will request post-incident RCA from cloud.
eric: status check — is traffic back to normal?

mike: SRV error rate down to baseline across all zones, consul elections stable for >15m, coredns pods healthy. marking incident as mitigated but keeping on-call for 1hr.
jess: creating incident page and will schedule a postmortem. brief notes for postmortem: cause = AZ egress/router flapping -> packet loss -> consul raft heartbeat timeouts -> leader election loop -> CoreDNS negative caches -> SRV lookup failures surface to services. mitigation = leader pin + heartbeat bump + coredns rolling restart.
support-bot: Notified affected customers at 03:25Z. update sent to account teams.
eric: thanks everyone. action items logged: (1) add per-AZ consul heartbeat thresholds (owner: eng-ml? no, eng-infra) (2) tune coredns negative-caching defaults for SRV (owner: eng-runtime) (3) add cross-alert linking consul election spikes with DNS SERVFAILs (owner: eng-sre).

eric: incident declared resolved at 03:26Z. will follow up with postmortem doc and timeline. :white_check_mark:
